It is done, and submitted. You can play “Survival of the Fittest” yourself—that is, see what the world is capable of—and then, if you’re so inclined, take a look at my own system. If you’re into that and have time left over, click on “Life Is a Process” and see how my evolutionary philosophy is structured. Finally, if you like—or like people who write books—you can download a free version of my third book. But that’s for you.

But if you just want to watch people being, well, eaten, well… okay.

The meat-juicer (what all animal lovers will first recognize him for, I’m sure) is clearly visible—I think I used at least 150 medium zombies to make life difficult for him—but not his weapon. He’s far more powerful than one human one-armed soldier can possibly withstand, so I thought a better hiding spot would be above ground. Not a bad idea until you see what is down there, and what else…

If you want to know what it’s like for a zombie to be “Eaten Alive,” start at the beginning of the video. But, seriously, how many of us eat at this (pardon the pun) rate?

We tend to think that living organisms are “good”. “Well this life, is at least better than that life,” we say. But food consumption patterns, consumption of meat, all over the world, are engaging in practices that are killing others so that we can indulge ourselves. This is a bit of a paradox, isn’t it? If our body is in fact made up of many “people”, and if it is not good for people to be inborn “Eaten Alive”, why have we got so fixated on treating some others as inferior meat? The “survival of the fit” that we’re doing should, if nothing else, make you ask “What does my body want?”

The game will be uploaded on June 2nd, so that is when I will stop updates. Thank you to everyone who contributed to this project!

I have finished the cutscenes for the game, and uploaded them to Youtube. The cutscenes for now are here, and hopefully I will get them linked up in the game tomorrow.

It is done, and submitted. You can play “Survival Author’s Guide to Self-Care After Publication” on the Guizmo Kids Publishing app now! The free game is a part of Guizmo’s efforts to promote reading and writing in children with low literacy skills.

I will post the game details on my blog on Monday of next week. I’m waiting for the app store update today. Please share with your family, friends and children. They’ll love the game.

I love Survival Author’s Guide to Self-Care after Publication, and I think everyone who loves kids either writing or reading will too.

You might want to print and play with your child right away. I recommend you will like it. The game is a cute way to refresh ideas of self- care for published authors on a quick and short trip, or when you are in a car in a hurry, or need some light and playful fun.

And guess what? You will not be the same person with 8 puppies and 100,000 dollars after publishing. You can turn out to be a very depressed but also very tired author after that.

That’s why in addition to survival techniques for happy self-care, publishing in Guizm Kids also provides a free 30-day writing and publishing workshop in guismop.com after you sign up for our membership in guizmop.com. The workshop can help you to get out of this rabbit hole immediately.
